newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian defence chiefs bring calm to northwest.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian defence chiefs bring calm to northwest.

text.p: Calm returned to Cambodia's Battambang province on Saturday after the country's co-defence ministers helped defuse tension between rival factions in the coalition government, officials said.

Co-defence ministers Tea Banh of the Cambodian People's Party (CPP) and Tea Chamrath of the royalist FUNCINPEC party chaired a meeting on Friday in Battambang involving senior police and military officers and representatives of Cambodia's rival premiers.
"Everything is OK now, after the meeting," Tea Banh told Reuters on Saturday, without elaborating.
The meeting was called to end several days of clashes in the rice-bowl province of Battambang in northwest Cambodia between CPP and FUNCINPEC forces, in which both sides received casualties.

Representatives of both parties, which formed an uneasy coalition after U.N.-run general elections in 1993, presented evidence to show the other had provoked the clashes, said Thlang Sovanarith, FUNCINPEC's deputy military commander of the region.
He said both sides had tried to block main roads leading into Battambang on Friday, saying the measure was aimed at preventing civilian casualties.
"But from yesterday afternoon, we have stopped fighting. This morning the situation is calm," he told Reuters on Saturday, adding that roads in the area were safe and clear.

FUNCINPEC and CPP troops clashed this week in Battambang's Moung district, sources from both sides said. The fighting was linked to Khmer Rouge defectors, with some of the former guerrillas siding with the CPP and some with FUNCINPEC.
Human rights workers in Battambang said on Friday they had reports that 14 CPP soldiers and two from FUNCINPEC had been killed in the last three days.

Rival premiers Ranariddh of FUNCINPEC and Hun Sen of the CPP had been expected to discuss the problems in Battambang and a draft electoral law during a cabinet meeting on Friday. But the meeting was postponed at the request of Hun Sen.
The fighting in Battambang marked the most serious friction between the two sides since clashes in November left several people wounded.
